newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Valecom registers for CVRD sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Valecom registers for CVRD sell-off.

text.p: Valecom, one of two consortia due to bid in the privatization auction of Brazilian state mining giant CVRD, has registered with the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange to qualify for the sell-off.

Valecom said in a statement it had delivered the necessary documentation, which includes a list of its members and financial guarantees for three billion reais ($2.83 billion), to the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange clearing house.

Consortia interested in bidding in the April 29 auction of a 40-45-percent voting stake in CVRD at a base price of three billion reais ($2.83 billion) have until 1830 local time/2130 GMT to register with the stock exchange, a bourse spokeswoman said. Valecom is led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, which have equal stakes in the consortium amounting to more than 50 percent jointly.
A group of 11 Japanese steelmakers and trading companies led by Nippon Steel Corp have a joint 10-percent stake in the group.

The group of Japanese investors comprises Nippon Steel Corp, NKK Corp, Kawasaki Steel Corp, Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd, Kobe Steel Ltd, Nisshin Steel Co Ltd, Nakayama Steel Works Ltd, Nissho Iwai Corp, Mitsubishi Corp, Itochu Corp and Marubeni Corp.

Brazilian metal and metallurgical group Caemi, 40-percent-owned by Japan's Mitsui & Co Ltd, is also a member as are two Brazilian pension funds, Centrus and Sistel, which have an existing joint stake in CVRD of 2.8 percent.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
